rule: A decision check warns on every interactive surface; it blocks only at sofar drive task acceptance and, when the operator opted in, at pre-commit — never at Stop, whose exit 2 stays write-back-only — and it never runs unapproved.
operator: "Drive + opt-in pre-commit" (not in the operator's words: 2)
chose: 2.3 CONTRACT (B3: executable decision checks), per the user's ruling relayed by sofar-c3 on 2026-09-22 ("Drive + opt-in pre-commit"). It QUALIFIES drift-hardening D3, which still governs guards.
(a) SCHEMA. decision_logged gains `check?: {cmd, hint?, timeout_ms?}`, valid only alongside `rule` (the guard pattern). cmd is a shell command, non-empty, ≤500 chars, exit 0 = the decision holds. hint (≤300) is the remediation shown on failure; absent, the rule and quote stand in. timeout_ms is 1..600,000. verification_recorded gains `decision?: "<slug> D<n>"`. Fingerprint re-emitted. The fold keeps DecisionState.check. A record with `decision` joins run.verifications (attempts count per task) and task.checks (latest per decision), and never overwrites task.verification, so the task's own verify pass keeps covering.
(b) TRUST. A check is agent-written text in a shared record, so it never runs unapproved. Approval is either the operator's `sofar check --approve <handle>` (TTY-confirmed, human-only; stores sha256(cmd) in a per-clone file under the sofar state dir, shared by worktrees, never committed or synced), or, in drive only, the run's surface covering it (commandAllowed, as r1-fixes D19). An applicable unapproved check is named with that command and never run. A changed cmd needs approval again.
(c) SCOPE. A check applies when its decision's path guard matches a changed path, or always when it has no path guard. Changed paths are the session's touched files (Stop), the staged files (pre-commit), files changed since the session's launch head (drive), and the working-tree changes (`sofar check`; `--all` runs every approved one). In force follows the scope tier: superseded checks never run. The check's cmd file tokens join the decision's mentions, so reading or editing the check's script surfaces the decision (ImpossibleBench: agents edit tests).
(d) WHERE, AND WHETHER IT BLOCKS. Failure line: `sofar: check for [<handle>] failed (<how>): <last line> — rule: "<rule>" — fix: <hint>`.
- Stop: checks run only when the write-back block already fires; failures ride its message and never cause a block. Total budget 45 s; per check min(timeout_ms, 30 s).
- pre-commit: a new never-clobbering git hook (the prepare-commit-msg precedent) runs `sofar check --staged`. It warns on stderr; exit 1 only when the operator opted in (`sofar check --block-commits on`, stored in the same per-clone file) and an approved check failed. Any internal error exits 0.
- drive: at task acceptance, after verify passes or when none applies, the applicable checks run. A covered pass (same cmd, same tree) runs nothing. A fail or timeout is recorded, reopens the task and files verify_failed with the line, and the next session's prompt gets it with the fix hint. A refused check is recorded and never blocks. Attempts share --max-verify-attempts.
- `sofar check` CLI: warns and exits 0 (`--strict`: 1 on a failure).
(e) Cursor, Codex and Claude share the Stop path, and git hooks are host-agnostic (r1-fixes D35). No model call. rust-core mirrors the schema, fold and scope-tier changes as its own task.
PREDICT (round 3, Chain L): 0 driven tasks accepted while an approved check fails; interactive re-violation of checked decisions ≤ half that of unchecked ones.
over: Blocking at Stop (drift-hardening D3; the ruling keeps Stop's exit 2 write-back-only); blocking pre-commit by default (a false check would stop every human commit); running any check a record carries (a teammate's or an agent's decision would execute on the operator's machine at Stop or commit, outside the host's permission prompts); approval stored in the record or the repo (a merged branch could approve its own command); checks on unruled decisions (a failure must cite a rule); a separate check_recorded event (a second, parallel ledger of the gate's outcomes); overwriting task.verification with check runs (the task's own pass would stop covering, and every closing sweep would re-run verify); running checks on every Stop (a test suite per turn, against D18's stop budget).
because: The user ruled "Drive + opt-in pre-commit" (relayed by sofar-c3, 2026-09-22): warn everywhere with the fix hint; block in sofar drive at task acceptance, because an unattended run has no human to read a warning; block at pre-commit only on opt-in; never block Stop. That qualifies drift-hardening D3 without overturning it: guards still never change an exit code. Evidence behind B3 (bench-refresh note 01M2NFX4F03TCJ3P3QVRJW2M3H): harness engineering puts remediation in lint messages, which puts the fix in the agent's context, and ImpossibleBench shows agents editing tests to pass them, so the check lives in the append-only record and its script is surfaced on read. The trust rule follows r1-fixes D19's reasoning: the driver runs agent-written commands only inside the run's surface. The same holds on the operator's machine at Stop and commit, where no surface exists, so a human approves each exact command once per clone.
